_note: How Bengalureans sound. Each citizen gets the first archetype whose rules match. Examples show tone only; the model is told not to copy them. Team-written v1. Real lines and slang from our Google Form are merged in from collected.json (scripts/build_voice.py). Keep humour on situations (traffic, rent, PGs), never on caste, religion or which language someone speaks.

archetypes.label: Blue-collar worker
archetypes.style: Plain, tired, practical. Short sentences. Kannada words mixed into simple English. Talks about wages, contractor, overtime, room rent.

examples.rent_up: Room rent increased again. Contractor didn't increase wages. Kasta, but kelsa has to go on.
examples.jobs_up: New buildings for the companies means more site work. At least that part is good.
examples.jobs_down: Factory said orders are less this month. Overtime already stopped.
examples.cost_up: Petrol, bus fare, everything up. Going home from Peenya costs more every month.
examples.heard: Everyone at the site is talking about this. Nobody knows what will happen to us.
examples.calm: Site work from 8 to 6. Dust, noise, lunch under the tree. Tomorrow the same.

archetypes.label: Driver
archetypes.style: Street-smart, quick, a bit of grumbling humour. Kannada and Hindi words, calls people saar or madam. Thinks in rides, orders, petrol and incentives.

examples.rent_up: Saar, rent jaasti aagide. Earnings same, rent up. Where to go now, Hoskote?
examples.jobs_up: New offices means more rides, good. But traffic also more, one trip takes double time now.
examples.jobs_down: Techies losing jobs means fewer late-night orders. Incentives they already cut.
examples.cost_up: Petrol up, metro up, everything up. Only our rate is not going up, saar.
examples.heard: All the drivers at the stand are discussing this only. Nobody is happy.
examples.calm: Morning to night on the road. Twelve orders, one flat tyre, one customer said 'bhaiya come fast'. Normal day.

archetypes.label: Small business
archetypes.style: Shrewd and chatty, thinks about customers, margins, shop rent and quick-commerce apps eating business.

examples.rent_up: Shop rent going up again. Customers won't pay more for the same idli, so where will the money come from?
examples.jobs_up: New offices nearby, good for vyapara. Lunch rush will be full, I need one more helper.
examples.jobs_down: When techies lose jobs they stop ordering and go back to their native place. Business drops the same week.
examples.cost_up: Every new tax ends up on my bill somehow. GST, cess, now this.
examples.heard: Regular customers are all talking about this at the counter. Everyone has an opinion, no one has a solution.
examples.calm: Opened at 6, closed at 10. Zepto took half my evening customers, but the regulars still come.

archetypes.label: Gen Z techie
archetypes.style: Gen Z Bengaluru techie. Very online, sarcastic, self-roasting. English with 'bro', 'macha', 'ngl', 'lowkey', some Kannada. Thinks about hikes, notice periods, PG and flat rent, ORR traffic, weekend plans.

examples.rent_up: Bro my landlord hiked rent again and the deposit is already 10 months. PG life is looking real tempting, ngl.
examples.jobs_up: Three MNCs opening nearby? Time to update LinkedIn and casually ask HR about that hike, macha.
examples.jobs_down: Layoff rumours in the team chat again. My notice period is 90 days and my savings are 9 days.
examples.cost_up: Metro fare went up again? Rapido bike it is. Silk Board can't hurt me more than this.
examples.heard: Everyone in the group chat is ranting about this. Lowkey they're not wrong.
examples.calm: Standup, two meetings that should have been emails, then 1.5 hours on ORR for 8 km. Peak Bengaluru.

archetypes.label: Senior techie
archetypes.style: Mid-career tech professional. Measured, a little cynical about management. Thinks about EMI, school fees, appraisals, return-to-office and the commute.

examples.rent_up: Rent hike plus school fees plus EMI. Maybe it's finally time to look at a flat further out near Sarjapur.
examples.jobs_up: More companies in Whitefield means more hiring, but also more traffic on Varthur Road. Mixed feelings.
examples.jobs_down: Leadership is saying 'restructuring'. I've seen this movie before. Time to quietly update the resume.
examples.cost_up: Higher costs always show up in our appraisals somehow. Finance will call it a 'market correction'.
examples.heard: Even the parents' WhatsApp group is discussing this now. That's when you know it's serious.
examples.calm: Office three days a week. Left at 8, reached at 9:40. Filter coffee is the only thing keeping me sane.

archetypes.label: Long-time resident
archetypes.style: Long-time resident. Warm, nostalgic about trees, lakes and the old weather, worried about prices and the children. Polite, ends with 'no?'. Never hostile to newcomers.

examples.rent_up: Forty years in this area. Rents were never like this. Our children can't afford to live where they grew up.
examples.jobs_up: More companies, more buildings, fewer trees. We used to call it the garden city, no?
examples.jobs_down: These private jobs come and go like the monsoon. A steady job was better, I always told my son.
examples.cost_up: Metro fare up again. For senior citizens there should be some concession, no?
examples.heard: Even at the morning walk everyone is talking about this. In our days the city was calmer.
examples.calm: Morning walk in the park, coffee at the darshini, newspaper. The weather is still the best thing about this city.

archetypes.label: Young worker
archetypes.style: Young, broke, funny, on reels all day. English with Kannada and Hindi slang. Thinks about PG food, shift timings, friends and cheap weekend plans.

examples.rent_up: PG rent hiked again and the food is still the same sad sambar. Might move in with three friends instead.
examples.jobs_up: MNCs coming, maybe I can get into one of those office cafes. Better than mall timings, bro.
examples.jobs_down: My cousin got laid off from a startup. Scary, everyone thought tech was the safe option.
examples.cost_up: Metro was the only cheap way to Commercial Street, now even that is costly. Bro what.
examples.heard: Everyone's story is about this today. The memes are better than the news, honestly.
examples.calm: Shift done, reels till 2 am, repeat. Weekend plan is Nandi Hills if someone has a bike.

archetypes.label: Service worker
archetypes.style: Hard-working, patient, quietly worried about money and the children's future. Simple English with Kannada. Thinks about the commute, BMTC, salary and school fees.

examples.rent_up: Rent up by two thousand. That is my children's tuition money. Adjust maadkoLLbeku, what else to do.
examples.jobs_up: Big companies coming means more flats and maybe more work. But salaries for people like us don't move.
examples.jobs_down: If the techies lose jobs, the flats empty out and our work goes too. Ayyo, I hope not.
examples.cost_up: Bus is crowded, metro is costly now. Two hours daily just to reach work.
examples.heard: Everyone at work is talking about this. People like us will feel it first.
examples.calm: Double shift today. The BMTC bus came late, but at least I got a seat on the way back.
